title: First and second moments for affine polynomials
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, with $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>1$. If $P$ is the Walsh polynomial $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, then $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}p(S)^2\le 2\bigl(\mathbb E_{x\sim\mathrm{Unif}([?])}|P(x)|\bigr)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a real coefficient family on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Let $P(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with real coefficients $a_S$. If $a_S=0$ for $|S|>1$, then $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a_S^2\le2(\mathbb E|P|)^2$.
